subtitle: The heart of modern music production. DAWs provide the software environment for recording, editing, mixing, and mastering your musical creations.

introduction.title: What is a DAW?
introduction.text: A Digital Audio Workstation is software that serves as the central hub for music production. It integrates multitrack recording, MIDI sequencing, audio editing, mixing, and often includes virtual instruments and effects.

columns.title: Core Functions
columns.text: Recording: Capture audio and MIDI. Editing: Cut, copy, paste, time-stretch. Mixing: Balance levels, EQ, effects. Sequencing: Program MIDI instruments. Automation: Control parameters over time. Export: Render final mixes and masters.

columns.title: Key Components
columns.text: Timeline: Arrange tracks in time. Mixer: Control individual track levels. Browser: Manage files and sounds. Piano Roll: Edit MIDI notes visually. Plugin Host: Load instruments and effects. Transport: Play, record, stop controls.

cards.title: Avid Pro Tools
cards.description: Industry standard for professional audio. Excellent audio editing capabilities, advanced mixing and automation, collaborative workflows.
items: Best for: Professional recording studios, audio post-production

cards.title: Apple Logic Pro
cards.description: Excellent value with included content. Intuitive Mac-native interface with comprehensive virtual instruments and high-quality effects.
items: Best for: Mac users, songwriting, electronic music, home studios

cards.title: Ableton Live
cards.description: Unique session view for live performance. Excellent for electronic music with innovative audio manipulation tools and loop-based workflow.
items: Unique session view for live performance
Best for: Electronic music, live performance, sound design

cards.title: FL Studio
cards.description: Pattern-based sequencing with lifetime free updates. User-friendly interface excellent for hip-hop and EDM production.
items: Best for: Beat making, electronic dance music, budget-conscious producers

cards.title: Cockos Reaper
cards.description: Extremely affordable and lightweight. Highly customizable interface with powerful scripting capabilities and low system resource usage.
items: Best for: Budget-conscious producers, audio editing, older hardware

fields.label: GarageBand
fields.value: Free with Mac, great for beginners

fields.label: Tracktion T7
fields.value: Full version free, older but capable

cards.title: Consider Your Needs
items: Music Style: Different DAWs excel at different genres
Workflow: Linear vs. loop-based vs. session-based
Platform: Windows, Mac, or Linux compatibility
Collaboration: File sharing and compatibility needs

cards.title: Try Before You Buy
items: Start with free options (GarageBand, Reaper trial)
Watch tutorial videos for different DAWs

cards.title: Recording & Editing
items: Tracks: Individual audio or MIDI channels
Regions/Clips: Recorded or imported audio segments
Comping: Creating perfect takes from multiple recordings
Time Stretching: Changing tempo without pitch
Pitch Correction: Tuning vocal and instrumental parts

cards.title: Mixing & Processing
items: Automation: Recording parameter changes over time
Sends & Returns: Routing for effects processing
Freeze/Commit: Converting MIDI or processed audio

cards.title: Learn Keyboard Shortcuts
cards.description: Master the essential shortcuts for your DAW. This dramatically speeds up your workflow and keeps you in the creative flow rather than hunting through menus.

cards.title: Organize Your Projects
cards.description: Use consistent naming conventions, color coding, and folder structures. Create templates for common project types to speed up startup.

cards.title: Save and Backup Regularly
cards.description: Set up automatic saving and maintain multiple backups. Consider cloud storage for important projects and use version control.

cards.title: Optimize Performance
cards.description: Learn buffer size settings, freeze tracks with heavy processing, and keep your system optimized for audio production.
